messages:
Ryan H: Observed a perf regression after the driver restart on prod — KV cache hit rate for >512 seqlen requests dropped from ~65% to ~20%. Logs show massive miss thrash. Anyone looked at how our cache keying interacts with hot model/kernel reloads?
Maddie L: Saw the same alarm. I think when we flip kernel selector flags we generate a new runtime_kernels_version and that gets folded into the cache key today, so restart = full invalidation.
Jia Chen: We need to decide a persistence/invalidation policy. Persisting across restarts is great for hit rate, but unsafe if kernel ABI or model version changes.
Tom S: Suggestion for deterministic keying: composite key with explicit fields: model_id:model_sha:kernel_tag:seqlen_bucket:batch_shape:device_slice. Example: `gptj-6b:abcd1234:cuda12_2-fastattnv3:seq512:bs1:g0` — that way keys only invalidated when one of those fields changes.
Riley K: We can also add a driver generation token appended to keys like `driver_gen=2028` that we bump on driver start. That allows eager invalidation when desired.
Maddie L: Two operational modes: eager purge on restart (drop all keys with stale driver_gen) vs lazy validation (keep persisted keys but validate first lookup against model/kernel checksums). Lazy lowers cold-start cost but risks subtle incompatibilities if we don't validate.
infra-bot: deploybot: rollout started for runtime v2.4.0 (kernels: fast-attn-v3) :information_source:
Jia Chen: For persistence store I prefer RocksDB with per-prefix LRU + TTL, plus small compact values. Value schema: `kv_len|last_access_ts|meta_flags`. Keep serialized payload minimal to reduce write/read overhead.
Ryan H: Quick sim I ran locally to compare approaches:
```
# sim results (micro)
mode,eager_purge,lazy_validate,persist+gen
hit_rate,0.10,0.48,0.82
p95_ms,2200,1100,980
```
Persist+gen gives the best steady-state hit rate; lazy_validate reduces cold-start pain but slower long-term.
Tom S: Important safety note: persisted keys can be incompatible after kernel ABI changes. We must ensure `kernel_tag` encodes ABI checksum (not just a friendly name). Otherwise we might serve incorrect kv entries silently.
Maddie L: Invalidation for model changes should be atomic from the control plane side: bump a `model_gen` prefix when the model_sha changes and queue background deletion of old prefixes rate-limited so we don't spike IO.
Riley K: Tombstone approach looks good: mark old prefixes expired, let background sweeper purge keys, and maintain a metric for #stale_serves so we can detect accidental stale-serving.
Jia Chen: Operational metrics to add: `kv.hit_rate_by_seqlen_bucket`, `kv.persistence_stale_count`, `kv_eviction_rate`, `kv_write_latency`, and `kv_background_sweep_progress`. We need dashboards and alerts for unusual increases.
Ryan H: Action items I'm proposing: (1) implement composite key format including explicit `kernel_tag` (Tom), (2) add `driver_gen` and lazy invalidation toggles (Riley), (3) persist with RocksDB + background sweeper (Jia), (4) add metrics/dashboards (Maddie). I'll open the umbrella PRs and link issues.
Tom S: Also add an emergency runtime flag `runtime.kv.strict_invalidation=true/false` so SRE can force eager purge on incidents.
Maddie L: +1 to the flag. We should also ship a small migration tool to rewrite keys when we rotate kernel ABI intentionally.
Riley K: Test plan: simulate driver restarts, simulated model rollouts with kernel ABI bumps, and ramp long-sequence traffic to measure rewarm times. I'll draft the test harness.
Ryan H: I'll create tickets and assign. @Maddie L @Tom S @Jia Chen @Riley K please ack and I'll schedule a 30m sync to align PRs. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: ticket created: INF-3421 "KV cache autoinvalidate + persistence plan" (assignee: Maddie L)
Riley K: I'll add test cases to INF-3421 and include the sim script.
Maddie L: Thanks — we should prioritize the kernel_tag checksum and the emergency flag first.
Ryan H: Sounds good. I'll start PRs for key format and the runtime flag today.
Tom S: FYI I'll prototype the RocksDB layout and expose a compact index for prefix deletes.
Jia Chen: I'll draft the dashboard panels and add the metrics exporters.
Ryan H: Great. Closing thread for now — follow-ups in INF-3421 and PRs.
